title: Add an Index: Speed Up Search
description:
**SITUATION:**

The customer "My orders" lookup (`WHERE customer_id = ...`) is slow on production-sized data. `orders` holds about 300,000 rows here and has no index on `customer_id`, so Postgres reads every row.

Your ticket is at `~/ticket/TASK.md`. Connect with `psql` (database `quickbite`, role `learner`).

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the lookup from your ticket and note the `Seq Scan`.
2. Create an index on `orders (customer_id)`.
3. Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` again and confirm the plan uses the index.

**SPEC:**

- A valid, plain index on `orders` whose first column is `customer_id`
- The lookup's plan uses `Index Scan` / `Bitmap Index Scan` / `Index Only Scan`, no `Seq Scan on orders`
- The table keeps all its rows
- Graded from the catalog and a live `EXPLAIN`

hints: You are the `learner` Linux user on a dev box with PostgreSQL running locally. Run `psql` to open the `quickbite` database (PGDATABASE is already set).
Read `~/ticket/TASK.md` first: dates, thresholds and ids are different in every session.
Run the ticket's `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` before and after; compare `Execution Time`.
problemStatement.overview: Add an Index: Speed Up Search
problemStatement.brief: Add an Index: Speed Up Search
problemStatement.solution:
## 1. See the problem

Use the customer id from your ticket:

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, status, total, created_at FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1234;
```

```text
Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..6197.00 rows=120 ...)
  Filter: (customer_id = 1234)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 299880
Execution Time: ~30 ms
```

`Seq Scan` means Postgres read every row. `Rows Removed by Filter` shows how much work was thrown away.

## 2. Create the index

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_id ON orders (customer_id);
```

Check it exists:

```sql
\d orders
```

## 3. See the fix

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, status, total, created_at FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1234;
```

```text
Bitmap Heap Scan on orders ...
  ->  Bitmap Index Scan on idx_orders_customer_id
        Index Cond: (customer_id = 1234)
Execution Time: ~0.2 ms
```

If the planner still seq-scans (rare on a fresh table), run `ANALYZE orders;` so it has fresh statistics.

## Trade-offs

- Indexes speed up reads on that column and slow down writes slightly (each `INSERT`/`UPDATE` maintains them) and use disk.
- Index the columns you filter, join, or sort on a lot, not every column.

Then **Submit**.
